caveats: PARTIAL: covers lectures 1-19 of 20. Do not cite this KB as covering CS221 as a whole. The Bayesian networks unit is covered in full (lectures 12-14: definition, exact inference, explaining away, rejection sampling, Gibbs sampling, the Markov blanket, conditional independence, and learning the parameters by count and normalize, Laplace smoothing and expectation maximization). The logic unit is covered in full (lecture 15: propositional logic, syntax, semantics, entailment, Ask/Tell, satisfiability, modus ponens, soundness and completeness; lecture 16: first-order logic, its syntax and semantics, propositionalization, modus ponens with substitution and unification, and translating English into first-order logic). Lecture 17 (an introduction to language models: the tensor and probabilistic views, n-grams, why model language, scaling laws, architecture, pre- and post-training, RLHF, tokenization, systems, and the state of the field) is covered. Lecture 18 (AI and society: why technologists should care, dual use, benefits/misuse/accidents, the ecosystem view, inequality, alignment, copyright and fair use, openness and transparency) is covered. Lecture 19 (a guest lecture on the economics of AI: the dual lens of technology and organizations, the compute, data and distribution supply chains, general-purpose technologies, the J-curve, GDP and growth) is covered. Lecture 20 (the closing fireside chat) is not covered.

Figure descriptions were written by vision-capable subagents (deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp) because the parent model (deepseek-v4-pro) cannot perceive images. The chart- and text-dense figures were then audited by a second vision pass, which corrected four errors: a circle radius (2 → 1.4, matching the source code's boundary), a scatter point count (25 → 20), a graph line colour (red → green), and an invented monkey inside a magnifying-glass illustration.

Lecture 6 figures were described by a single vision pass, cross-checked against source-derived values instead of a second vision audit: the 8-puzzle Manhattan distances sum exactly to the lecture's 1+1+3+1+1+1+1+3 = 12, and the A* counterexample's modified costs reconcile exactly with the code arithmetic (e.g. C→D: 1 + 0 − 1000 = −999).
The SVM-with-polynomial-kernel video in lecture 4 was described from 7 sampled frames of 43, not watched in full.

At ≈45:21 of the lecture 6 transcript the lecturer says the bad heuristic gives a modified cost of −9999; the slide figure shows −999, which is what the definition computes. Both readings are preserved (transcript as spoken, slide file as printed).

Lecture 7's two graphviz figures (flaky tram, dice game) were vision-passed against the rendered PNGs and matched the draw_graph source exactly (no discrepancies). The two distance plots are described from their exact data (traced from executing the lecture's code), not from images.

The deck (language_models.pdf, pinned at caa93be) was committed two days after the lecture and is the only version that exists, so small differences from what was on screen in class cannot be ruled out, though the transcript follows it closely. The deck prints no slide numbers; 'slide N' in this KB is PDF page N. Its pages were read as images by claude-sonnet-5-5 in three parallel parts; two further claude-sonnet-5-5 passes audited 18 chart-, table- and screenshot-heavy pages at up to 600 dpi and found five chart-description errors (Kaplan figure line extents, Chinchilla dot count and Gopher-budget line, the DCLM pipeline's 12.3% band, the GPT-3 chart's x spacing, one table underline), all corrected and the two reversals confirmed by the parent (claude-opus-5-5). The lecturer's spoken numbers differ from the slides in three places, recorded in the transcript header and the wiki page ('7 billion' for the 70B model; 'four bytes per word' for a 144 TB figure that is 4 bytes per token; 'about three trillion' for 3.71T tokens). The transcript edit was parent-adjudicated: 104 markers identical, paragraph word ratios 0.76-1.04, number inventory clean apart from removed false starts and H100 restorations, 20 [Ed: unclear] markers.

Lecture 19 (Economics of AI; the course schedule calls it 'AI Supply Chains') is a guest lecture by Rishi Bommasani, introduced by Percy Liang, and was built like lecture 17: parent claude-opus-5-5, deck reading, figure audit and transcript copy-edit delegated to claude-sonnet-5-5. Its deck is a live Google Slides document, not a file in the lecture repo, so it cannot be pinned: it was transcribed from a PDF export taken on 2026-10-26, nearly a year after the lecture. The transcript follows the export slide by slide, but at one point the lecturer says he mislabelled a slide whose exported title is already correct, so the deck may have been edited after the lecture. Several names are spoken but printed nowhere in the deck (Daron Acemoglu, David Autor, Dario, Sam, Arvind and Sayash); the transcript restores their spelling from the captions with inline notes, and the slides show the forecasters' photographs without names. Where the lecturer's numbers differ from the slides (0.5 and 0.9 vs. 0.55% and 0.90%; about a hundred billion dollars vs. $97B), both are reported.
